title: End of WW1 & Versailles Adventure
welcome_lead: By 1918 the war is ending. Then the world has to agree what to do next — at Versailles in 1919. 🌹
meta_desc: End of WW1 Adventure — a KS3 walkthrough of the Armistice, Versailles and the legacy of the war.
final_note: You saw the Armistice on 11 November 1918, the Treaty of Versailles 1919, and why this peace did not last.

walkthroughs.body_html:
In April 1917, the USA joined the war on the Allied side after German submarines sank American ships.

By 1918, Germany was running out of soldiers, food and fuel. Sailors mutinied; people protested at home. The Kaiser fled to Holland.

The fighting stopped at 11 a.m. on 11 November 1918. This is still remembered every Remembrance Day. 🌺

In 1919, the winners met at the Palace of Versailles near Paris.

The Treaty of Versailles was very harsh on Germany. Key terms:

  • Germany had to accept war guilt (Clause 231).
  • Germany lost land — like Alsace-Lorraine to France.
  • Its army was cut to 100,000 men.
  • It had to pay reparations of around £6.6 billion.

Germans were furious. Many called it a 'diktat' — something forced on them.

WW1 cost about 17 million lives in total.

It created new countries — like Poland, Czechoslovakia and Yugoslavia. The League of Nations was set up to keep peace, though it had no army of its own.

But anger in Germany helped pave the way for Hitler to come to power in 1933 — and only 20 years later, Europe was at war again.
